+---
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8780'
+title: Put both spawn paths on the Extras process runner, and give the shell pass its limits
+---
+## What
+
+This package starts a process in two places, and the two do not have the same safety.
+
+- `Sources/FoundationModelsSkills/Resources/ScriptProcessRunner.swift` — a process group, a timeout, `SIGKILL` of the group, and the tail of the output. Used by `run script`.
+- `Sources/FoundationModelsSkills/Render/ShellInjection.swift:203-214` — `Process()` with `/bin/sh -c`, then `readDataToEndOfFile()` and `waitUntilExit()`. **No timeout. No limit of the output. No process group. No kill.**
+
+Thus a `` !`sleep 1000` `` in the body of a skill stops the render for ever, and a command that writes without end fills the memory of the host. The `run script` path is safe; the render pass is not. Also, neither path registers its pid with `ProcessRegistry.global` of `FoundationModelsExtras`, which is the backstop of the family against a leaked group.
+
+1. Delete `Resources/ScriptProcessRunner.swift`. Use the `ProcessRunner` of Extras (card ^86z4bmc on that board), which holds the group, the timeout, the caps and the registry.
+2. `RunScript` calls `ProcessRunner`. Its behavior, its result fields and its correctives do not change.
+3. `ShellInjection` calls `ProcessRunner` also, and it gets the limits that it never had:
+   - a timeout for each command, with a default that this package sets;
+   - a limit of the bytes of the output;
+   - the process group and the kill.
+4. **What the render shows when a command fails a limit.** The pass writes the same inert marker that it writes when the policy turns the shell off, with the reason. It does not write the partial output, and it does not stop the render of the rest of the body.
+5. The timeout and the byte limit are fields of `RenderPolicy`, thus a host can change them, and the default is safe.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] No file of this package spawns a process; both paths call the Extras `ProcessRunner`.
+- [ ] A shell command that passes the timeout does not stop the render: the pass writes the marker and the render continues.
+- [ ] A shell command that writes more than the byte limit does not grow the memory: the read stops at the limit.
+- [ ] After a timeout, no child of the command is alive.
+- [ ] `run script` gives the same results as before, with the same fields and the same correctives.
+- [ ] The default timeout and the default byte limit are in `RenderPolicy`, and a host can change them.
+- [ ] `swift build --build-tests` gives 0 warnings, and `swift test` is green.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsSkillsTests/ShellInjectionTests.swift`: a body with a command that sleeps longer than the timeout gives the marker, and the test completes in about the timeout.
+- [ ] Same file: a command that writes more than the byte limit gives the marker, not the output.
+- [ ] Same file: a body with one slow command and one fast command renders the fast one.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsSkillsTests/RunScriptTests.swift`: the results that are asserted now do not change.
+- [ ] `swift test` — all tests pass, 0 failures.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
+
+#process-safety #skills #cross-repo
\ No newline at end of file

+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m2xgqvahhd63cwsfgqyty0fw
+  text: |-
+    ### Research
+
+    Read the real signatures in `.build/checkouts/FoundationModelsExtras` at `2123cdf`.
+
+    - `ProcessRunner.run(executable:arguments:workingDirectory:timeout:outputCap:registry:) async throws -> Outcome` — `timeout` is a `Duration`, `registry` defaults to `.global`, thus both paths get the registry backstop free.
+    - `Outcome` carries `termination` (`.exited(code:)`, `.signaled`, `.timedOut`), `duration`, `lineCount`, `output` (the kept tail), `isTruncated`.
+    - `OutputCap(lineCount:byteLimit:)`. `ProcessOutputTail` splits on `\n`, and a final newline adds no empty line — the same rule as the `splitIntoLines` of this package, thus the line counts of `run script` do not move.
+    - `Failure.spawnFailed(status:)` and `Failure.waitFailed(errno:)` are the two throws.
+
+    `ProcessRunner.run` is `async`. `ShellInjection.render` is `sync`, thus the render path must become `async`. A blocking bridge (a semaphore over a `Task`) is refused: `RenderPipeline.renderBody` runs on the cooperative pool through `UseSkill.execute`, and a blocked cooperative thread for each parallel render can starve the pool.
+
+    The plan:
+
+    - Split the pass protocol: `RenderPass` stays synchronous for passes 1 and 3; a new `ShellRenderPass` carries the `async` pass 2. `renderMetadata` stays synchronous, thus `metadata()`, `commandListing()` and every catalog reader keep their signatures.
+    - `RenderPipeline.renderBody`, `SkillsRegistry.call(id:arguments:)` and `SkillsRegistry.preloadedBodies()` become `async`. `UseSkill.execute` is already `async`. The README block must hold `preloadedBodies()` in a `let` before the `Instructions` builder, because a result builder takes no `await`.
+
+    The card text names marketplace grants. Card ^8mxhn6a removed that concept: the gates now are the host `RenderPolicy` and the per-skill `allowed-tools` grant only. The code is followed as it is now.

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m2xj6ek4n3jxevdrkqm8r06y
+  text: |-
+    ### Implementation landed
+
+    `Sources/FoundationModelsSkills/Resources/ScriptProcessRunner.swift` is deleted. No file of this package starts a process any more: both paths call `FoundationModelsExtras.ProcessRunner`, thus each command gets the process group, the group `SIGKILL` at the timeout, the output cap, and the `ProcessRegistry.global` entry.
+
+    `ShellInjection` gets the two limits from `RenderPolicy`: `shellCommandTimeout` (30 seconds by default) and `shellOutputByteLimit` (1,048,576 by default). A command that passes either limit writes no output into the body. The pass writes the inert marker of that limit in its place -- `timedOutMarker` or `outputOverTheLimitMarker`, which read like the `disabledMarker` that was already there -- and the render of the rest of the body goes on.
+
+    `RunScript` keeps every field, every value and every corrective. The tail is still the last 32 lines, each one formatted `"{n}: {text}"`, and the byte limit of one run is 1 MiB.
+
+    The async ripple, as the research comment states:
+
+    - `RenderPass` stays synchronous for passes 1 and 3. A new `ShellRenderPass` carries the suspending pass 2. `IdentityRenderPass` conforms to both, thus its one synchronous `render` still stands in for any of the three passes.
+    - `RenderPipeline.renderBody`, `SkillsRegistry.call(id:arguments:)` and `SkillsRegistry.preloadedBodies()` are `async`. `renderMetadata` stays synchronous, thus `metadata()`, `commandListing()` and every other catalog reader keep their signatures.
+    - `QuarantinedText` gained `mappingOriginalSpans(awaiting:)`. Both walks share `spansWithPrecedingCharacters`, because Swift has no `reasync`.
+    - The README block and its test copy read `preloadedBodies()` into a `let` before the `Instructions` builder, because a result builder takes no `await`. The demo does the same.
+
+    Two findings that came out of the work:
+
+    - `StringProtocol.splitIntoLines` lost its last caller when `ScriptProcessRunner` went, thus it is deleted. `ReadResource` names the rule in its doc comment now, not that symbol.
+    - `SkillsRegistry.renderedFallback` lost its second caller for the same reason, thus `renderedMetadataText` holds the two lines itself.
+
+    The documents are corrected: `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/development.md` (the deviation record), `README.md` and the two `plan.md` code blocks.
+
+    The card text names marketplace grants. Card ^8mxhn6a removed that concept. The code as it stands has two gates only -- the host `RenderPolicy` and the per-skill `allowed-tools` grant -- and the work follows the code.
